run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T07:02:55Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by HTTP 504/500 responses the proxy returns for requests to the frontend upstream. The proxy's own access log shows 504 'UT response_timeout' after 15000 ms on GET /api/products/*, GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout, and its ingress error spans (~1349.8 in the 75-minute window) all end at ~15.0 s. Tracing the failures down one level: the frontend's /api/checkout route returns HTTP 500 with '13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #...' from checkout, and checkout's client span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct fails with gRPC status 14 and 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer' after 8.4-42.6 s. product-catalog itself stopped serving: its server-span volume fell from ~3005 per 5 min (06:57:55 bucket) to 2284, then 98.9, then 0, and its container log stream ends at 07:08:08.5 with no lines afterwards, while the pod stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts and the deployment was not rolled out. Coinciding with the onset, the only chaos-controller events in the namespace are 17 'Updated' events on PodNetworkChaos/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 from 07:00:54 to 07:08:54, i.e. the network path of the product-catalog pod was being manipulated right when its traffic collapsed. The supported explanation is a network-level disruption of the product-catalog pod that made its gRPC calls hang and be reset, propagating timeouts/500s through frontend to frontend-proxy; the exact chaos fault type cannot be read with the allowed APIs, and product-catalog's equal log silence (including its 10 s 'Reloading Product Catalog...' lines) leaves a secondary process-level-freeze hypothesis open.

claims.text: frontend-proxy produced 1349.77 error-status ingress spans and 21.34 error-status 'router frontend egress' spans in the 75-minute window ending 07:18:32Z, against 17729.97 non-error ingress spans, so its own error signal is real and not merely an alert artifact.

frontend-proxy's own access log shows upstream timeouts: e.g. "POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000 -, "GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout 15000, and "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=..." 504 UT response_timeout 15000; 1069 of 6015 log lines read between 06:55:00Z and 07:09:15Z matched the 504/500 pattern.

The proxy's error spans are ~15 s upstream timeouts: sampled frontend-proxy ingress error spans carry http.status_code 504 with durations such as 15000895, 15000869 and 14999950 us (mostly 504, with one 500 at 8549452 us), and the paired 'router frontend egress' span carries error=true with http.status_code 0 (no upstream response).

The error burst started in the 5-minute bucket ending 07:02:55Z, matching the alert start: frontend-proxy error-span increases per 5 min were 3.29, 1.11, 0 and 4.44 for the buckets at 06:42:55-06:57:55, then 151.11 (bucket 07:02:55), 592.22 (07:07:55) and 501.75 (07:12:55).

A whole failing trace (load-generator 'user_add_to_cart', trace ed1fe3f47eba414a393fa2e55bf21a42) shows the propagation path: load-generator GET 504 at 15.002 s -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 at 15.000895 s -> 'router frontend egress' error=true/http 0 at 15.0007 s -> frontend GET span lasting 15.000255 s.

frontend returned HTTP 500 on POST /api/checkout (98.52 and 98.59 error spans for 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout') with exception message '13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"6E92ZMYYFZ"' / '#"OLJCESPC7Z"' / '#"0PUK6V6EV0"' / '#"1YMWWN1N4O"', and its grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client span shows rpc.grpc.status_code 13.

checkout's calls to product-catalog are the failing leaf: checkout span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct carries error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and status description 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer', lasting 8540618-42607159 us (8.4-42.6 s) across all 5 sampled checkout attempts.

product-catalog stopped serving during the incident: its span count per 5-minute bucket fell from 3005.56 (bucket at 06:57:55), 3140.0 (06:47:55) and 3204.44 (06:52:55) to 2284.44 (07:02:55), 98.89 (07:07:55) and 0 (07:12:55).

product-catalog's container log stream stops at 2026-11-15T07:08:08.521Z: only 4 lines exist between 07:08:05Z and 07:18:32Z ('Product Found', 'Reloading Product Catalog...', 'Loaded 10 products', 'Product Found') and none afterwards; the earlier lines returned for 07:01:34-07:08:08 contain routine 'Product Found' and 'Reloading Product Catalog... / Loaded 10 products' entries with no error text.

The only chaos-controller events in otel-demo during the incident target the product-catalog pod: 17 events with involvedObject PodNetworkChaos/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9, reason Updated, message 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource', timestamps from 07:00:54Z through 07:08:54Z (roughly every 30-60 s).

product-catalog was not restarted or re-deployed: pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 is Running, ready=true, restartCount 0, container started 06:25:07Z, with no lastState termination; deployment product-catalog has 1 desired/1 ready/1 available and condition NewReplicaSetAvailable since 06:25:07Z, so the same image/replica set was in place during the window.

Namespace-wide object state shows no other pod damage: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running and ready, and the only container with a terminated lastState in the namespace is fraud-detection (reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 06:57:09Z, restartCount 2); all 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False.
Error span counts per service over the 75-minute window: frontend-proxy 1371.11, frontend 282.48, recommendation 3.05, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 1.02, and 0 for accounting, cart and payment.

fraud-detection was OOMKilled at 06:57:09Z (exitCode 137) and its container restarted at 06:57:10Z (3 Created/Started events, restartCount 2); its logs before the kill show normal Kafka record consumption ('Consumed record with orderId ... updated total count to: 837') with no application error.

product-catalog was still answering some calls during the early disruption: spans read for service product-catalog between 07:05:00Z and 07:12:00Z include successful oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct spans with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and durations of 106-130 us (e.g. at epoch 1794726341 s, 1794726309 s, 1794726301 s), so the disruption was partial/intermittent rather than a total process death from the first moment.

frontend-proxy itself was neither restarting nor saturated at pod level: its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d is Running with restartCount 0 and deployment frontend-proxy is 1/1 ready/available, and its 504s are explicitly logged as 'UT response_timeout' (upstream timeout) after 15000 ms rather than proxy-generated connection errors.

Primary hypothesis: a network-level disruption injected on the product-catalog pod is the deepest supported cause of the alert. Its onset (PodNetworkChaos Updated events from 07:00:54Z) precedes the error burst (bucket ending 07:02:55Z), coincides with the collapse of product-catalog server spans (3005->2284 in that same bucket, then 98.9, then 0) and with callers seeing 'connection reset by peer' from 100.64.188.136:8080; the chaos spec (fault type: delay/loss/partition/corrupt) could not be read, so the exact mechanism is unproven.

Secondary hypothesis, not resolved: the product-catalog application process itself also stalled, beyond pure network isolation. Its own periodic 'Reloading Product Catalog... / Loaded 10 products' lines (every ~10 s up to 07:08:08Z) stop entirely after 07:08:08.521Z while the pod still reports ready=true with 0 restarts, which a pod-network fault alone would not obviously explain; process-level telemetry (CPU, thread state) was not available to confirm or refute a freeze.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart at 06:57:09Z. It is a real event in the window, but every observed failing checkout transaction names product-catalog ('failed to prepare order: failed to get product #...'), fraud-detection accumulated only 1.02 error spans in 75 minutes, and its log after restart shows normal Kafka consumption, so nothing ties it to the product-catalog error path.

Rejected as the cause: a faulty frontend-proxy binary/config or a proxy pod restart. The proxy pod has restartCount 0, its deployment is 1/1 available with no rollout in the window, and its 504 entries are labelled 'UT response_timeout' with 15000 ms upstream time, i.e. downstream waits on frontend, matching frontend's own 500s and 15 s spans.

Read the PodNetworkChaos object for pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 (namespace otel-demo) to determine its action, mode, direction and duration, and confirm when or whether the experiment ended, since the chaos CRD is not reachable with the permitted tools.

Verify whether product-catalog recovered after 07:12:55Z (new server spans, resumed 'Product Found'/'Reloading Product Catalog...' logs) and whether frontend-proxy's error rate returned to its pre-07:00 baseline of ~0-4 error spans per 5 minutes.

Investigate why product-catalog stopped emitting its internal 10 s reload log lines while its pod stayed Ready with 0 restarts; capture container CPU/thread state or a goroutine/profile dump if the pod is still silent, and confirm what its readiness probe actually checks.
Treat the fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137, 06:57:09Z) as a separate reliability item and review its memory limit; it is not the cause of this alert.

gaps: The Chaos Mesh custom resources (PodNetworkChaos/NetworkChaos/PodChaos) are not among the readable kinds, so the injected fault type, direction, target selectors and duration could not be inspected; only the controller's 'Updated' events are visible.
Prometheus span-metric data ends at ~07:12:55Z and Jaeger data at ~07:10:24Z, so whether product-catalog and frontend-proxy recovered after that is unknown.

No pre-incident baseline for frontend-proxy error rate exists in the data: the error-span query over 2026-11-14T19:00Z-2026-11-15T06:02:55Z returned no series (status no_data), and the alert rule 'RequestErrorRate' was not listed by list_prometheus_rules (status no_data), so comparison is limited to the 06:42:55-06:57:55 buckets inside the same window.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total has no ERROR series for checkout or product-catalog (only frontend, frontend-proxy, ad, recommendation, fraud-detection and zero-valued accounting/cart/payment were returned), so service-level error-rate coverage for checkout and product-catalog is missing; their errors are evidenced only from Jaeger traces.

frontend's own container logs could not be read: the log query for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64blr returned no lines (status no_data), so the 500 responses are evidenced from spans only, not from frontend application logs.

The product-catalog error-filtered log query returned no matching lines (status no_data) and the rpc_server_duration_milliseconds metrics query returned no data, so product-catalog's server-side error counters and grpc status labels remain unknown rather than zero.
Product-catalog process-level state (CPU, memory, thread/goroutine state) is not observable with the available tools, and the pod/deployment objects reflect 07:19Z state, not the incident instant.
The change_history integration is not available, so what created or modified the PodNetworkChaos resource cannot be verified.

Services not examined for their own error/latency signals: currency, email, shipping, quote, image-provider, kafka, load-generator (beyond its 504 client spans), otel-collector, flagd, postgresql, valkey-cart; their status is unknown rather than healthy.
next_steps: Inspect the PodNetworkChaos resource for product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 (action, mode, duration, direction) and confirm whether the experiment ended at ~07:08:54Z.
Check post-07:13Z product-catalog traffic and logs plus frontend-proxy error rate to confirm recovery and bound the incident end.
Compare frontend /api/products and checkout PlaceOrder latency histograms against a known-good period before 07:00Z to quantify added delay, if such a baseline is available.
Determine why product-catalog's internal periodic reload logging stopped at 07:08:08Z while the pod stayed Ready.
Review fraud-detection memory limits as a separate change, unrelated to this alert.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then.
